description: Tested a more selective weak-label regularization family than focal downweighting: kept strong label smoothing at 0.01, but increased smoothing only on the weak focal stream to 0.02 while leaving the strong site-conditioned stream crisp. This still regressed hard to 0.75931133 from 0.77805835. The effect matches other weak-focal-weakening ideas: without_focal/amphibian/insect rise, but bird/with_focal crater. So the current focal subset is not merely too noisy in target sharpness; selectively softening weak labels pushes the model away from the balanced optimum.

asi.hypothesis: Applying stronger label smoothing only to the weak focal stream will reduce noisy bag-label dominance without blurring the scarce strong site-conditioned labels.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc regressed sharply because selectively softening weak focal targets over-rotated the model toward the hard subsets at the expense of bird/with_focal.
asi.next_action_hint: Prune selective weak-focal label softening alongside weak-focal downweighting. The next experiments should move away from weakening the focal stream uniformly and look for a different family entirely.
asi.takeaway: The incumbent does not benefit from making the weak focal stream uniformly softer; the present focal objective strength is part of the load-bearing balance.

description: Tested a new regularization-axis variant on the incumbent baseline: keep the tuned anchor strength, but shift the anchor target itself upward from the old 18% fallback prior to 20% (`site_blend_anchor_prob=0.20`). This regressed clearly to 0.76799399 from 0.77805835 and moved the peak later to step 400. So the anchor target is not stale in the same way the anchor strength was; pulling the site-blend parameters toward a more shared-heavy prior over-softens the current optimum.

asi.hypothesis: After shrinking the site bank and strengthening the anchor, the optimal fallback prior itself may have shifted upward from the old 18% anchor target.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc regressed and the later peak indicates the stronger shared fallback prior over-regularized the current site-conditioned optimum.
asi.next_action_hint: If the anchor-target axis is revisited, only test the downward side (less shared fallback than 18%), not higher. The current result says the incumbent does not want a more shared-heavy prior.
asi.takeaway: The useful retuning after `K_SITE=6` was in the anchor strength and optimizer speed, not in moving the fallback prior upward.

description: Completed both directions of the new site-blend anchor-target sweep by lowering the fallback prior from 18% to 16% while keeping the tuned anchor strength and blend LR fixed. This also regressed clearly to 0.76509928 from 0.77805835. The lower prior shifted the model toward the hard subsets (without_focal/insect) at the expense of bird/with_focal, so the anchor target itself now looks pinned too: neither 16% nor 20% beats the old 18% prior.

asi.hypothesis: If the incumbent did not want a more shared-heavy anchor target, it might instead prefer a lower fallback prior than 18%, letting site conditioning dominate a bit more under the stronger anchor.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc regressed sharply; lowering the anchor target over-rotated the model toward the hard-subset side of the tradeoff.
asi.next_action_hint: Treat the anchor-target axis as pinned at 18% on the incumbent baseline. Future search should move off site-blend prior tuning entirely.
asi.takeaway: The current optimum is tight not just on anchor strength and LR but on the anchor target itself; the old 18% fallback prior still wins.

description: Completed the opposite side of the new focal-loss weighting family by *upweighting* the weak focal BCE slightly to 1.05 while keeping the incumbent star-schema baseline fixed. This also regressed badly to 0.75323722 from 0.77805835. The failure pattern was surprisingly similar to the weakening experiments: bird/with_focal collapsed instead of improving, while amphibian/without_focal stayed high. So the focal-stream scalar-weight family is now pruned on both sides; the current labeled-loss balance is not meaningfully improvable by a uniform rescale of the weak focal objective.

asi.hypothesis: If downweighting weak focal labels hurt because the focal stream became too weak, a small upweight might instead recover bird/with_focal enough to improve the overall proxy.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc regressed sharply and the focal upweight did not even produce the expected bird/with_focal recovery.
asi.next_action_hint: Prune uniform weak-focal weighting entirely. Future objective changes should avoid whole-stream rescaling and instead target a more structured distinction than 'all focal labels up or down together'.
asi.takeaway: The weak focal stream is load-bearing in a more structured way than a single scalar weight can capture; both 0.9 and 1.05 are clearly worse than 1.0.

description: Tested a new star-schema optimizer axis on the incumbent baseline: gave the site-bank parameters (`site_head.*`) a modestly faster 1.5× LR while leaving the projection/species bank/global LR unchanged. This regressed clearly to 0.76546044 from 0.77805835. The model lost bird/with_focal without compensating gains elsewhere, so the smaller `K_SITE=6` site table is not under-optimized by step 300; speeding up the site-bank parameters destabilizes the coupled optimum rather than helping it.

asi.hypothesis: After shrinking the site bank to 6 prototypes, the site-bank parameters may need a slightly faster optimizer than the rest of the model to express the new capacity regime before the step-300 checkpoint.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc regressed materially because the faster site-bank learning weakened bird/with_focal without producing useful gains on the harder subsets.
asi.next_action_hint: Prune site-head-specific LR increases for now. The remaining headroom is probably not in making the site bank learn faster under the current objective.
asi.takeaway: The beneficial `K_SITE=6` change is a capacity effect, not an optimization-speed bottleneck in `site_head.*`.

description: Ablated the update-magnitude trust term on the fully retuned incumbent by disabling the `site_blend_delta_coef · ||M_cond-M_shared||` contribution and falling back to the anchored per-site scalar only. This came fairly close but still regressed to 0.77765890 from 0.77805835. So the trust term remains useful even after all the later `K_SITE=6` / anchor / blend-LR retuning; the older tiny gain was not washed out by the newer improvements.

asi.hypothesis: The current incumbent may no longer need the original RMS update-magnitude trust term after the stronger site-bank and site-blend retuning, so a simpler anchored scalar fallback could match or improve it.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc stayed below the incumbent, showing the update-magnitude trust term still contributes a real if small gain on top of the retuned baseline.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the RMS update-magnitude trust term in the incumbent. The trust family seems solved at 'plain detached RMS only'; future search should not revisit trust ablations unless a genuinely different conditioning mechanism emerges.
asi.focus: architecture / trust-term ablation on incumbent baseline
asi.takeaway: The current best still depends on the plain RMS update-magnitude trust signal; removing it gives back a small but real gain.

description: Attempted to run the incumbent S22 audit through a custom `scripts/train.py` command, but the autoresearch harness rejected it because `autoresearch.sh` exists and must be used for experiment runs. No model training was executed.

asi.hypothesis: Directly running the incumbent config on S22 via `scripts/train.py` would let us measure whether the fast-proxy incumbent still matches the historical S22 fold.
asi.rollback_reason: Harness policy: when `autoresearch.sh` exists, experiment runs must go through that wrapper.
asi.next_action_hint: Adapt `autoresearch.sh` to support S22 and LOSO audit modes, then rerun through the wrapper.

description: Added audit support to `autoresearch.sh` (custom split names, generic metric names, and LOSO-result parsing) and used it to run the fast-proxy incumbent on the true S22 decision fold. Result: the 0.778 dev incumbent does **not** carry over to S22; it lands at only 0.71813097, below the earlier v4 S22 reference (~0.761). The profile is exactly the old S22 pathology: bird/with_focal are very strong, but `without_focal` collapses to 0.657 and amphibian to 0.566. This strongly suggests the fast-proxy trajectory has drifted toward the custom dev split rather than making thesis-wide progress.

asi.hypothesis: If the fast dev proxy is faithful, the incumbent that scores 0.778 on `S13,S15,S19` should still land in the ~0.76+ range on the original S22 decision fold.
asi.audit_axis: generalization audit / incumbent on true S22 fold
asi.result_interpretation: The proxy gain does not transfer to S22. This is evidence of benchmark drift rather than robust progress.
asi.best_step_shift: S22 peak moved to step 1100 instead of the proxy's usual step 300, so the checkpoint-selection story also changes off-proxy.
asi.infrastructure_change: Kept a small `autoresearch.sh` enhancement so future S22/LOSO audits can run through the harness cleanly.

description: Attempted the full-LOSO audit with an inline `CKPT_SUBDIR=$(date ... )` shell expansion ahead of `bash autoresearch.sh`, and the harness rejected the command as nonstandard. No training ran.

asi.hypothesis: The incumbent should be audited on full LOSO through `autoresearch.sh` with the same settings used for the S22 audit.
asi.rollback_reason: Harness rejected the command form before training started.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry the LOSO audit through a simpler `VAR=... bash autoresearch.sh` command without inline shell substitutions.

description: The first full-LOSO audit attempt through `autoresearch.sh` failed immediately because the wrapper still passed several stale CLI flags (`--site-blend-anchor-prob`, `--cal-lr-mult`, `--site-head-lr-mult`, `--strong-mixup-alpha`, `--weak-focal-weight`, `--freeze-step`, `--phase2-lr`) that no longer exist in the current `scripts/train.py` after rollback. No training ran.

asi.hypothesis: The incumbent can be audited on full LOSO through the wrapper once the wrapper matches the actual current training CLI.
asi.rollback_reason: Wrapper/train CLI drift caused an argument-parse failure before training began.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the wrapper in sync with the live training script, then rerun the LOSO audit.

description: Ran the fast-proxy incumbent on full 9-fold LOSO through the audit-enabled wrapper. The result is a decisive collapse: pooled LOSO AUROC is only 0.39487338, with `without_focal=0.1345` and `insect=0.0887`, even though the embedded S22 fold still lands at 0.7213 and matches the direct S22 audit. This strongly settles the user’s question: the 0.778 dev trajectory is benchmark drift, not robust progress. The proxy-selected regime is massively over-specialized to the custom dev split and fails catastrophically once all held-out sites are considered.

asi.hypothesis: If the fast dev split is a faithful proxy, the incumbent tuned to 0.778 there should still produce a reasonable pooled LOSO score and at least roughly preserve its S22 behavior.
asi.audit_axis: generalization audit / incumbent on full 9-fold LOSO
asi.result_interpretation: The proxy is not faithful enough for continued blind local search. S22 itself is already down at 0.721, and pooled LOSO collapses much further to 0.395 because the hard held-out-site subsets fail catastrophically.
asi.next_action: Stop trusting incremental dev-split wins as evidence of thesis progress. Prioritize variance measurement and proxy repair before further microtuning.
asi.best_step_note: LOSO aggregation has no single meaningful `best_step`, so `best_step=0` is a sentinel placeholder for logging continuity.

description: Re-anchored the current proxy incumbent under the cleaned wrapper after the audit work. The exact historical dev result reproduces bit-for-bit at 0.77805835 with the same subset metrics and best_step=300, so the wrapper cleanup did not perturb the proxy benchmark. This serves as seed-0 of the requested variance audit.

asi.hypothesis: Before measuring seed variance, rerunning the incumbent under the cleaned wrapper should reproduce the known dev baseline exactly.
asi.result_interpretation: Proxy benchmark is reproducible under the current harness; any upcoming seed spread is due to initialization rather than wrapper drift.
asi.context: This proxy reproducibility now sits alongside the new evidence that the proxy itself does not transfer to S22/LOSO.

description: Seed-1 of the requested variance audit (`SEED=43`) on the exact proxy incumbent collapsed from 0.77805835 to 0.72321463. This is not millipoint noise; it is a 0.055 AUROC swing, with strong degradation on `without_focal`, amphibian, and insect, and the peak shifting to step 400. So the recent run-to-run headroom on the proxy is dominated by initialization variance, and the last many micro-keeps are far below the actual noise floor.

asi.hypothesis: If the proxy incumbent is stable, alternate seeds should stay within a few millipoints of 0.778 rather than changing the conclusion of recent micro-keeps.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc regressed massively under a seed change, revealing that the proxy has high initialization variance.
asi.next_action_hint: Prioritize finishing the seed-replicate audit before any more microtuning. Aggregate over multiple seeds or change the benchmark protocol; otherwise 1e-3 gains are meaningless.
asi.takeaway: The fast proxy is extremely seed-sensitive in the current regime; recent micro-optimizations are not trustworthy as single-seed wins.

description: Seed-2 of the variance audit (`SEED=44`) again collapsed far below the nominal 0.778 incumbent, landing at 0.71914810. This is consistent with the seed-43 result rather than the seed-42 high outlier: `without_focal`, bird, and insect all soften materially, and the best checkpoint again moves to step 400. Two alternate seeds now say the recent single-seed micro-keeps are deep inside the noise / initialization-variance band.

asi.hypothesis: If seed-43 was a fluke, another alternate seed should rebound close to the nominal 0.778 proxy incumbent.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc remained dramatically below the incumbent, reinforcing that the proxy is highly seed-sensitive rather than merely suffering one bad draw.
asi.next_action_hint: Continue the seed audit before touching model knobs. If more seeds stay near 0.72, treat seed-42 as the outlier and reconsider the entire recent optimization trajectory.
asi.takeaway: The first alternate seed was not an anomaly; the proxy incumbent is unstable across random seeds.

description: Seed-3 of the variance audit (`SEED=45`) fell even further, to 0.67385913. The failure is now unambiguous: the supposed 0.778 incumbent is not a stable regime but a rare favorable seed, with `without_focal`, amphibian, and insect collapsing badly and the peak drifting later again to step 600. At this point the recent dev-split micro-trajectory is empirically invalid as a single-seed optimization story.

asi.hypothesis: If the proxy incumbent has moderate but tolerable seed variance, later seeds should still cluster near the low 0.7s rather than collapsing dramatically.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc collapsed far below the incumbent again, showing the regime is not just noisy but qualitatively unstable across seeds.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop interpreting single-seed proxy wins as progress. Finish the small seed panel, then pivot to proxy repair or multi-seed evaluation before any further architecture tuning.
asi.takeaway: The proxy-selected incumbent behaves like a lucky seed rather than a robust optimum.

description: Seed-4 of the variance audit (`SEED=46`) recovered slightly relative to seeds 43–45 but still landed only at 0.72752782, far below the nominal 0.778 incumbent. The distribution is now clear: one high seed at 0.778, one middling seed at 0.728, two low seeds near 0.72, and one severe failure at 0.674. This is much larger than the recent optimization deltas and confirms that the dev benchmark is dominated by seed variance rather than the micro-retunes we were making.

asi.hypothesis: Another independent seed may clarify whether the seed-45 collapse was an extreme outlier or part of a broad unstable distribution.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc remained well below the incumbent, confirming that seed sensitivity remains too large for single-seed proxy optimization to be trusted.
asi.next_action_hint: Prune single-seed dev microtuning as stale. Either finish the final seed replicate or pivot immediately to benchmark-protocol repair (multi-seed averaging, later checkpoint window, or streaming subsets).
asi.takeaway: The dev proxy's variance band is enormous relative to the claimed gains; recent local improvements are not decision-relevant.

description: Checkpoint-window repair test on the proxy incumbent: increased `PATIENCE` from 10 to 20 so training would continue validating beyond `unsup_warmup_end=1400` before early stopping. The result was bit-for-bit identical: dev_auroc stayed at 0.77805835 with the same subset metrics and best_step=300. So on the proxy itself, the early-stop window is *not* the reason later unsupervised pressure looks dead; the selected checkpoint already remains step 300 even when we allow substantially more post-warmup runway.

asi.hypothesis: The proxy may be prematurely declaring the post-warmup region dead because patience 10 stops too soon after the step-300 peak; increasing patience should reveal any later improvements.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric exactly tied the incumbent; extending the checkpoint-selection window alone did not change the chosen proxy checkpoint.
asi.next_action_hint: Treat proxy-side early stopping as stale for this specific incumbent. The checkpoint-window mismatch appears to be between proxy and S22/LOSO behavior, not a bug in proxy patience.
asi.focus: benchmark protocol / checkpoint-window extension on proxy
asi.takeaway: Extending patience past `unsup_warmup_end` is inert on the proxy; the later-checkpoint story is off-proxy, not a local early-stop artifact.

description: Started a new benchmark-protocol session that fixes the cache subset draw independently from model initialization. Added `--cache-subset-seed` plumbing through `scripts/train.py` and `autoresearch.sh`, then re-ran the incumbent with `SEED=42` and `CACHE_SUBSET_SEED=42`. The baseline reproduces exactly at 0.77805835, so the new protocol is backward-compatible while letting us decompose initialization variance from subset variance.

asi.hypothesis: If the previous 5-seed audit conflated initialization and data-subset noise, separating the cache-subset seed from the training seed will let us identify which source actually dominates the proxy variance.
asi.protocol_change: benchmark now supports fixed focal/unlabeled subset draws via CACHE_SUBSET_SEED independent of SEED
asi.result_interpretation: The new protocol faithfully reproduces the historical incumbent before any decoupled-seed audit is run.

description: First decoupled-seed audit under the new fixed-subset protocol: changed only model initialization (`SEED=43`) while holding the focal/unlabeled cache draw fixed (`CACHE_SUBSET_SEED=42`). dev_auroc still collapsed massively to 0.67853053 from 0.77805835. So the earlier variance was not mainly coming from different focal/unlabeled subset draws — initialization alone is enough to destroy the proxy result, with especially severe collapse on `without_focal`, amphibian, and insect and the peak drifting to step 600.

asi.hypothesis: If most of the previous 5-seed spread came from changing the cached focal/unlabeled subset along with initialization, then fixing `CACHE_SUBSET_SEED=42` should make `SEED=43` stay much closer to the baseline.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc still collapsed badly even with the subset draw fixed, so initialization variance remains a dominant failure mode.
asi.next_action_hint: Initialization variance is now confirmed as load-bearing. The next clean decomposition is the opposite direction: fix `SEED=42` and vary `CACHE_SUBSET_SEED` to measure the remaining subset contribution.
asi.focus: benchmark protocol / variance decomposition with fixed subset
asi.takeaway: The proxy is unstable even when the data subset is held fixed; the seed problem is not an artifact of cache-subsample coupling.

description: Second decoupled-seed audit under the fixed-subset protocol: held model initialization fixed (`SEED=42`) and changed only the focal/unlabeled cache draw (`CACHE_SUBSET_SEED=43`). This regressed to 0.76691128 from 0.77805835. So subset choice still matters, but much less than the initialization swing we just measured: changing only the subset costs about 0.011 AUROC here, versus ~0.10 when changing only initialization. The subset-only shift also follows the familiar tradeoff pattern, pushing toward without_focal/amphibian/insect and away from bird/with_focal.

asi.hypothesis: If the cache-subset draw is the main hidden overfitting channel, then changing only `CACHE_SUBSET_SEED` with `SEED=42` fixed should produce a collapse comparable to the earlier seed audit.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary dev_auroc regressed, though much more mildly than the initialization-only change, indicating that subset choice is secondary rather than dominant in the current variance story.
asi.next_action_hint: Update the ideas backlog: initialization variance is the first-order problem, subset choice is second-order but real. Future protocol repair should prioritize multi-seed evaluation before streaming-subset engineering.
asi.focus: benchmark protocol / variance decomposition with fixed initialization
asi.takeaway: Both sources matter, but initialization dominates: the fixed subset draw is not the main reason the proxy looked unstable.

description: Established a new stability-aware baseline by upgrading the benchmark to a 3-seed fixed-subset mean (`MULTI_SEEDS=42,43,44`, `CACHE_SUBSET_SEED=42`). The previous single-seed incumbent now averages only 0.71424504 under this protocol, with mean best_step drifting to 433.3. This baseline is much more faithful to the variance story than the lucky 0.778 single-seed number, so future comparisons should be made against this multi-seed mean rather than the old one-off peak.

asi.hypothesis: If initialization variance is the dominant failure mode, then a small fixed-subset multi-seed mean should provide a more trustworthy dev target than the old single-seed benchmark.
asi.protocol_change: new primary benchmark is 3-seed mean_dev_auroc with fixed CACHE_SUBSET_SEED=42
asi.result_interpretation: The robust baseline is ~0.714, not 0.778. This becomes the new yardstick for any stability-improving changes.
asi.next_action: Test whether slightly more conservative site-blend regularization/optimizer settings improve the multi-seed mean by sacrificing a bit of the lucky-seed peak.

description: Tested a more conservative stability-oriented retune under the new 3-seed fixed-subset benchmark by lowering `site_blend_lr_mult` from 5.3 to 5.0 while keeping the rest of the proxy-specific incumbent fixed. The multi-seed mean slipped slightly from 0.71424504 to 0.71356940, so the faster blend optimizer is not just a lucky-seed peak artifact; it still edges out the more conservative setting even under seed-averaging.

asi.hypothesis: Because initialization variance is now the main failure mode, a slightly slower site-blend optimizer might trade away lucky-seed peaks but improve the 3-seed mean by making training more stable.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary mean_dev_auroc regressed slightly under the new multi-seed metric, so the conservative blend-LR retune did not improve robustness enough to compensate.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep `site_blend_lr_mult=5.3` as the current multi-seed baseline. Future stability-oriented tests should look for genuinely different regularization levers rather than simply undoing the latest blend-LR gain.
asi.takeaway: The 5.3× blend optimizer remains marginally better than 5.0 even after averaging across seeds; instability is not fixed by just backing off this LR a little.

description: Tested a slightly stronger site-blend anchor (`1.2e-3` vs `1.1e-3`) under the new 3-seed fixed-subset benchmark, keeping the faster 5.3× blend optimizer. The multi-seed mean stayed essentially flat-to-slightly-worse at 0.71404598 versus 0.71424504. So making the site-blend prior a touch stronger does not materially improve robustness; the current multi-seed optimum is still centered very near the old seed-42 setting.

asi.hypothesis: If initialization instability comes partly from site-blend parameters moving too freely, a slightly stronger anchor toward the fallback prior might improve the seed-averaged mean even if it trims the lucky-seed peak.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary mean_dev_auroc did not improve; the stronger anchor was effectively neutral to slightly worse on the multi-seed benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Treat local anchor strengthening as close to solved under the multi-seed metric too. Future robustness work should move off tiny site-blend retunes and toward different protocol or architecture families.
asi.takeaway: The stability-aware optimum remains close to the old 1.1e-3 anchor; tiny extra regularization does not rescue the mean.

description: Tested the compressed mapped-Perch side branch under the new 3-seed fixed-subset benchmark by cache-compressing the raw ~14.8k Perch logits down to the 234 BirdCLEF species before transport, then enabling the zero-init Perch residual adapter (`INCLUDE_PERCH_LOGITS=1`) on seeds 42/43/44. This made the branch operationally cheap enough to run cleanly, but the result regressed hard to mean_dev_auroc=0.67819155 from 0.71424504. The failure mode is exactly the old concern: bird/with_focal become very strong while without_focal and insect collapse. So the problem was not just transport cost — even the cheap mapped-Perch signal is currently the wrong direction for this proxy.

asi.hypothesis: If the Perch side branch only failed before because the raw 14.8k logits were too expensive to move, then compressing them to BirdCLEF-mapped species probabilities at cache-build time might unlock a useful auxiliary signal under the new multi-seed benchmark.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary mean_dev_auroc regressed badly and the branch over-rotated toward bird/with_focal while collapsing without_focal and insect.
asi.next_action_hint: Prune the Perch residual branch for now, even in compressed mapped form. Future work should focus on protocol repair or genuinely different thesis-aligned objectives rather than Perch-logit side information.
asi.focus: feature branch / compressed mapped Perch logits under multi-seed benchmark
asi.takeaway: Transport was not the main blocker: the mapped Perch classifier signal itself is misaligned with the balanced proxy.

description: Tested the trust-term ablation under the new 3-seed fixed-subset benchmark by disabling the `site_blend_delta_coef · ||M_cond-M_shared||` contribution while keeping the rest of the multi-seed baseline fixed. The result stayed extremely close but still regressed slightly, from 0.71424504 to 0.71409253. So even under the stability-aware metric, the plain RMS update-magnitude trust term remains marginally useful; it is not just a lucky-seed artifact.

asi.hypothesis: Because the trust-term gain was tiny on the old single-seed benchmark, it might disappear or reverse once evaluated under the new 3-seed fixed-subset mean.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary mean_dev_auroc stayed slightly below the new baseline, so removing the trust term does not improve robustness enough to win.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the RMS update-magnitude trust term in the multi-seed baseline too. Future robustness work should move to different protocol or architecture families rather than revisiting this near-solved ablation.
asi.takeaway: The trust term survives the benchmark repair: it is still slightly useful even when lucky-seed effects are averaged down.

description: Upgraded the benchmark again from a fixed-subset 3-seed mean to a more drift-resistant 3-seed × 2-subset mean by adding `MULTI_CACHE_SUBSET_SEEDS=42,43` support to `autoresearch.sh`. Under this more robust workload, the old proxy-specific incumbent scores mean_dev_auroc=0.72343179 with mean best_step=400. This is a better yardstick than the fixed-subset-only mean because it averages both initialization noise and the secondary focal/unlabeled subset-draw effect.

asi.hypothesis: Since initialization dominates but subset choice still contributes some drift, a benchmark that averages over both seeds and cache-subset draws should be a more trustworthy optimization target than the previous fixed-subset mean.
asi.protocol_change: new primary benchmark is 3 seeds x 2 cache-subset draws (seeds 42,43,44 crossed with CACHE_SUBSET_SEED 42,43)
asi.result_interpretation: This becomes the new baseline for future robustness-oriented comparisons; it is less dependent on any single lucky initialization or single focal/unlabeled subset draw.
asi.next_action: Re-test only genuinely stability-oriented changes against this benchmark, not old single-seed microtunes.

description: Kept a benchmark-protocol refinement on the new 3-seed × 2-subset dev benchmark: increased validation cadence from every 100 steps to every 50 while holding the incumbent coupled regime fixed (K_SITE=6, site_blend_lr_mult=5.3, site_blend_anchor_lambda=1.1e-3, RMS update-magnitude trust, focal 17,408). mean_dev_auroc improved from 0.72343179 to 0.72399355. Unlike the old single-seed proxy where finer validation was inert, the multi-seed multi-subset benchmark benefits because different seed/subset draws peak at slightly different times; mean best_step moved to 391.7 and bird/insect both recovered while the harder subsets stayed comparable. This suggests some of the residual instability is now checkpoint-selection granularity rather than just architecture.

asi.hypothesis: A finer validation cadence may matter on the robust multi-seed multi-subset benchmark even though it was inert on the old single-seed proxy, because different seed/subset draws peak at slightly different steps.
asi.protocol_change: VAL_EVERY_STEPS 100 -> 50 on the current coupled incumbent
asi.context: K_SITE=6, K_SPECIES=8, site_blend_lr_mult=5.3, site_blend_anchor_lambda=1.1e-3, weight_decay=0, strong_stride=8, focal_cache_size=17408, unsup_cache_size=32768, unsup warmup still post-peak/inert.
asi.takeaway: Checkpoint granularity becomes load-bearing once the benchmark averages over multiple seeds and subset draws; the old conclusion that finer validation is inert no longer holds under the repaired benchmark.

description: Pushed the new checkpoint-granularity win further by tightening validation cadence from every 50 steps to every 25 on the same 3-seed × 2-subset incumbent. This regressed hard from 0.72399355 to 0.70998661. The mean checkpoint moved earlier to 345.8 and the model lost with_focal and bird sharply while only modestly helping without_focal, so the gain at 50-step validation was not monotone with denser evaluation. Too-frequent checkpointing appears to over-select early hard-subset-heavy snapshots rather than a balanced optimum.

asi.hypothesis: If 50-step validation helped because different seed/subset draws peak at slightly different times, an even finer 25-step cadence might capture another small multi-run gain.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary mean_dev_auroc regressed sharply; denser checkpointing over-selected earlier, less balanced snapshots.
asi.next_action_hint: Treat VAL_EVERY_STEPS=50 as a local optimum rather than continuing downward. If checkpoint protocol is revisited, try only coarser-than-50 or selection-rule changes, not denser validation.
asi.focus: benchmark protocol / validation cadence under robust benchmark
asi.takeaway: Checkpoint granularity matters on the repaired benchmark, but the optimum is non-monotonic: 50 helps, 25 overshoots.

description: Kept a coarser checkpoint-granularity retune after the 25-step overshoot: set validation cadence to every 75 steps on the 3-seed × 2-subset incumbent while holding the coupled regime fixed (K_SITE=6, site_blend_lr_mult=5.3, site_blend_anchor_lambda=1.1e-3, RMS update-magnitude trust, focal 17,408). mean_dev_auroc improved from 0.72399355 at 50-step validation to 0.72612057. The selection window moved later (mean best_step 425 vs 392), bird and with_focal both recovered materially, and without_focal/insect stayed strong enough to win overall. This clarifies the protocol story: the repaired benchmark wants finer checkpointing than 100, but not as fine as 25; 75 better balances the early hard-subset spikes against later bird/with_focal recovery.

asi.hypothesis: If 50-step validation improved the robust benchmark because 100 was too coarse, but 25 overshot by selecting early hard-subset-heavy checkpoints, an intermediate 75-step cadence may better balance those effects.
